races.title: State Senate, District 26
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Sarah Rascón
cands.bio: Democrat running for California State Senate District 26. Native Angeleno from El Sereno and UC Merced graduate. Worked as a field representative for Assemblymember Jimmy Gomez, a Deputy Executive Officer at the Mountains Recreation & Conservation Authority, and Director of County and Regional Affairs for Mayor Karen Bass.

endorsements.text: State Senator María Elena Durazo endorsed her, per the campaign website.
Planned Parenthood Advocacy Project Los Angeles County Action Fund endorsed her, per the campaign website.
Los Angeles County Firefighters Association Local 1014 is listed as an endorser on the campaign website.
Ballotpedia lists endorsements and voter-guide recommendations from the California Mountain Biking Coalition and several Sway voting groups, including 'Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress'.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Sarah Rascón holding an elected office, so there is no voting record. We found no documented actions or specific stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth limits, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, gun laws, abortion restrictions or school choice. Her campaign website lists priorities such as immigration, gun safety, corporate accountability and education, but those sections were collapsed and their text was not readable. Her exact birthplace is not stated beyond 'native Angeleno'. We found no news reporting or controversies about her.

local.label: Roots 100: She describes herself as a native Angeleno from El Sereno raised by her immigrant grandmother, and has worked in Los Angeles-area public service since college.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: She has no elected office on record. Her work has been in government and policy staff roles: field representative for Assemblymember Jimmy Gomez, Urban River Program Officer and then Deputy Executive Officer of Environmental Equity at the Mountains Recreation & Conservation Authority, and Director of County and Regional Affairs for Mayor Karen Bass. She also did community development organizing.
qual.why: She has no prior legislative service, but she has years of legislative-office and government policy work, which places her in the middle range. Her appointed planning commission seat and her board and delegate roles were not counted.

cands.name: Sara Hernandez
cands.bio: Democrat and Los Angeles Community College District trustee (Seat 4) since December 2022. Housing and environmental attorney, Valley College constitutional law instructor and former LAUSD middle school teacher. Founded the education nonprofit HYPE and worked in Los Angeles City Hall on housing and transportation.

endorsements.text: California Teachers Association, listed as an endorsement of her 2026 Senate campaign.
Sierra Club Angeles Chapter, listed as an endorsement of her 2026 Senate campaign.
YIMBY Action, listed as an endorsement of her 2026 Senate campaign.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Sara Hernandez was born or raised, or when she came to California. We found no record of specific actions she took as a community college trustee, such as sponsored measures or board decisions. We found no stated positions from her on data centers, property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, gun policy, H-1B visas or police pay. Her campaign platform page was cut off partway through, so any positions further down were not read. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey.

local.label: Roots 40: Her campaign site says she has lived in the 26th Senate District for over 20 years and describes generations of family history in California, but her own birthplace and upbringing are not stated.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Elected LACCD trustee in 2022. Practicing housing and environmental attorney, former LAUSD teacher, founder of the nonprofit HYPE, Los Angeles City Hall policy staffer on housing, transportation and infrastructure, and Valley College constitutional law instructor.
qual.why: She has held local elected office and has legal and city policy experience, which fits the middle range. She has no prior state legislative service or budget-writing role.
qual.label: She has held local elected office and has legal and city policy experience, which fits the middle range. She has no prior state legislative service or budget-writing role.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her campaign platform says 'we must build more housing. Full stop.' She calls for more density in high-opportunity neighborhoods, streamlined approvals and making sure cities follow state housing law.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her 2017 congressional campaign website said she is 'adamantly against vouchers and for-profit charter schools.' Ballotpedia quotes this.

pro-life.evidence: Her 2017 congressional campaign website said she would 'fight to protect Planned Parenthood and to abolish the Hyde Amendment.' Ballotpedia quotes this.

roots.summary: Her campaign site says she has lived in the 26th Senate District for over 20 years and describes generations of family history in California, but her own birthplace and upbringing are not stated.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Her platform says California is short on housing because of decades of underbuilding and that 'we must build more.' She supports more multifamily housing near transit and jobs, higher density, and streamlined approvals.
